topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines student learning outcomes, and frames the clinical and biological importance of cancer.

topics.label: Cancer as a breakdown of genetic regulation and tissue differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how genetic alterations and disrupted developmental differentiation programs lead to the failure of normal tissue architecture.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and benign-to-malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the distinction between benign and malignant tumors by detailing the histological and clinical features of tissue invasion and metastatic spread.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification conventions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic defines the systematic terminology used to name benign and malignant neoplasms based on their cell and tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic describes the local, structural, and systemic ways that primary and metastatic tumors cause clinical illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative cancer incidence across humans and other species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyse the frequency and mortality patterns of various cancers across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical methods of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the rationale, histological basis, and practical effectiveness of screening programs for early cancer detection.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the session by referencing the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping details for upcoming practicals and lectures.
